definitions.explanation: Used with negative verb forms to mean 'nothing at all.'
Used to indicate that something is unnecessary.

examples.japanese: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}には{何|なに}もない。
{何|なに}もそこまで{怒|おこ}らなくてもいいのに。
examples.english: You don't need to get that angry.
examples.notes: 何も + verb = there's no need to...

notes:
USAGE: {何|なに}も is always used with negative verb forms to mean "nothing" or "not anything." It cannot be used in affirmative sentences.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{何|なに}も{食|た}べない (to not eat anything)
・{何|なに}も{言|い}わない (to not say anything)
・{何|なに}も{知|し}らない (to not know anything)
・{何|なに}もない (there's nothing)
・{何|なに}も〜なくてもいい (there's no need to...)

CONTRAST:
・{何|なに}か (something - affirmative)
・{何|なに}も (nothing - negative)
